unit.why: A single long narrative, told by R. Zvi Hirsh of Zhidachov, about his visits to R. Barukh of Medzhybizh, the Seer of Lublin's visit there, the falling-out between the two tsaddikim, and Lublin forbidding his disciple to leave him.
unit.boundary_note: Running headers ('מהה"ק ר׳ ברוך ז"ל ממעזיביש') are interspersed in the text; the next division begins a separate teaching.

stories.start_quote: סיפר הה״ק מהר"צ מזידישוב אשר דרכו בקודש
stories.end_quote: והי׳ מסתופף בצלו עד יום פטירתו זי״ע
stories.summary_en: R. Zvi Hirsh of Zhidachov, a disciple of the Seer of Lublin, visits R. Barukh of Medzhybizh and witnesses his fiery recitation of the Song of Songs. The Seer then visits Medzhybizh, where the two tsaddikim clash over table talk, the daughter at the table and the circumcision honours, and are nearly drowned on the way home. When Zvi Hirsh later wants to leave Lublin for Medzhybizh, the Seer threatens to strip him of his spiritual levels, and he stays.
